name: Proof of Estimate (poe-solana)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 14 app (app/), static export, pointed at this devnet program. Only changes: base path, the IDL generated from the program source at the same commit (the committed app IDL is from a later program version), and /poll/?id= instead of /poll/[id] so it can be served statically.
learn: A forecasting poll stores the crowd's collective estimate on-chain: make_estimate takes a lower and upper bound, records the midpoint (lower+upper)/2 and the uncertainty (upper-lower)/100, and each poll lives at a PDA seeded by the global poll counter, so new polls get deterministic addresses.
source: programs/poe/src/contexts/create_poll.rs L21 (poll PDA = ["poll", num_polls le bytes])
steps: Clicked through the hosted app (test wallet 8WVm…): filled Create Poll and pressed Submit, which sent register_user + create_poll in one tx
Then moved the estimate slider on the new poll card and pressed Submit Estimate: make_estimate
register_user (mints 1000 POEKEN to the new user)
negative: register_user a second time for the same wallet is rejected (user PDA already in use, custom program error 0x0)
make_estimate with lower 70 > upper 30 is rejected (u16 underflow in upper-lower: program failed to complete)
ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): the new poll card then showed 'Yes 60%, 1 forecaster, 1 estimate' read back from devnet. Earlier read-only check: /poll/?id=0 shows the poll detail and estimate history.
limits: Resolving polls and collecting points need the poll's resolver; not exercised in this run.

name: Picassol (on-chain pixel canvas)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 12 frontend (frontend/), static export on devnet. Only changes: base path, devnet RPC, this program ID, and a 0-SOL fee on recolouring. Its MongoDB points API (pages/api) needs the author's database and is not hosted, so the points counter stays at 0.

name: TrustLock (dead man's switch)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 14 app, static export, pointed at a program we built from switch/ at this commit and deployed fresh to devnet on 2026-11-10. Only changes: base path, output: 'export' and the program ID.
learn: A dead man's switch is an escrow PDA seeded by ["escrow", owner, seed] that holds SOL until a deadline: the owner must check in before the deadline to push it back, and once the clock passes it, claim lets the beneficiary drain and close the account. The program reads the Clock sysvar, so the rule is enforced on-chain, not by the app.

name: sentient.send (winner-takes-all sentiment market)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js app as a static export, with this devnet program ID, the protocol authority set to our deployer, and base path /dapps/sentient-send/. Market pages are /market/?id=<address> instead of /market/<address>.
learn: A creator opens a market with 2–10 named sides and at least 1 SOL (2% fee, the rest split evenly across the sides). Anyone bets 0.01–1 SOL on a side until the end time. name: CipherVault (SOL multisig vault)
app_kind: The fork's own React + Vite app, unchanged except for the RPC (the fork points at a local validator), the IDL import (the committed IDL in app/src/anchor instead of target/, with this program's address) and base path /dapps/ciphervault/.
learn: A creator sets up a multisig with a list of owners and an approval threshold; its SOL sits in a program-owned vault PDA. Any owner can propose a SOL transfer (their own approval is recorded), other owners approve, and once approvals reach the threshold anyone can execute it, which moves lamports straight out of the vault.

name: stakes.wtf (stake for gov tokens, bribes, linear vesting)
app_kind: The fork's own React + Vite app (app/), with this devnet program ID, hash routing (#/vesting, #/create) for static hosting, and a small sha256 shim so spl-token 0.4 bundles. The program is built with the crate's own `testing` feature, so one program "day" is one second, and with the pool-creation fee receiver set to our deployer.
learn: Anyone opens a pool for a token (2 SOL fee). Stakers deposit the token and get gov tokens at the pool's gov price. Bribes are plain token transfers into the pool vault; sync_bribes credits a share of them to the pool each day, which raises what each gov token is worth. Unstaking burns the gov tokens and moves the tokens they are worth into a vesting position that unlocks linearly over 20 days.

instructions/unstake.rs and state/vesting_position.rs (burn, then 20-day linear unlock)

limits: This is the testing build (1 day = 1 second), so vesting and bribe shares that take days on mainnet finish in seconds here: the script's first claim after about 5 s paid 82.5 of 150, and the next one paid the rest. The app never calls sync_bribes, so bribes sent from the app sit in the vault until someone syncs (the script does). Create Pool in the app fails because its IDL is older than the program (no fee_receiver). Built with Solana 1.18.26 tools (platform-tools v1.41): the same source built with 2.3.13 tools failed at runtime with an access violation in initialize_pool, so the first deploy was upgraded.

name: Votara (DAO proposals, voting, quorum)
app_kind: The fork's own React + Vite app (client/votara-client), with this devnet program ID, hash routing (#/proposals, #/create, #/treasury, #/profile) for static hosting, and one bug fix: its TokenBalance read a connection context that is never mounted, which blanked the whole app on the profile page.
learn: A DAO account holds the config (voting period, quorum, approval threshold). Voters get voting power from stake_tokens or buy_tokens, anyone with a voter record creates proposals, each voter votes once (a vote-record PDA per voter and proposal), and after the voting period the DAO authority finalizes: under quorum is rejected, otherwise yes/(yes+no) against the threshold decides passed or rejected.

lib.rs L288-L358 cast_vote (one vote record per voter and proposal)

lib.rs L660-L684 buy_tokens (no SOL or token transfer either)

limits: stake_tokens and buy_tokens move no tokens and no SOL (the transfers are commented-out placeholders), so voting power is free: anyone can give themselves any amount up to the treasury's counter.
Quorum is an absolute count of unique voters (config.quorum_percentage, default 10), not a percentage.
We set the voting period to 40 s for the script and 150 s for the UI run, timelock 0 and quorum 2 (defaults: 7 days and 10 voters) with update_config, which the app has no screen for.
The proposal page's live counts come from a websocket log feed; on a plain HTTP RPC they stay at 0 until you reload, while the chain has the votes.
Only the DAO authority can finalize; on sol.college that is the test wallet m4Ac…, so other visitors can vote but not finalize.

name: Barn / OpenGrants (grant programs, milestones, payouts)
app_kind: The fork's own Next.js 14 app (app/) as a static export under /dapps/barn/ with this devnet program ID. The three per-account pages (/project/<pk>, /program/<pk>, /profile/<pk>) can't be pre-rendered for accounts made later, so they live at /project/view/?a=<pk> and so on. Profiles, programs, projects and milestones point at JSON metadata URIs; sample files are served from /dapps/barn/meta/.
learn: Each wallet makes one profile (an authority PDA keyed by the wallet points at a profile PDA keyed by a username). Sponsor profiles create grant programs and award one grant per project, in SOL (native mint) or an SPL token. Dev profiles add projects and milestones against their grant, submit them for review, and the sponsor accepts or sends them back (a reject instruction exists but, because of a bug, accepts); settle pays an accepted milestone from the sponsor's wallet, capped at the approved amount.

Our script's milestone #2 (Gy5XhNzwwXgq4dafotc27XtRVw6yv8MvCLeezGe6zXtk) is Accepted on devnet after its reject transaction; a post-run read confirms it.
approve_sponsor accepts any signer as "admin", so anyone can turn any fresh profile into a sponsor (the script shows an unrelated wallet doing it).
Settling a paid milestone a second time fails, but with ApprovedAmountExceeded when the cap check (which runs first) trips, so the error doesn't say the milestone was already paid.
Each wallet gets one profile on this program, ever (the authority PDA is keyed by the wallet).
The app shows names from each account's metadata URI; without one (or while the URI 404s) it shows "Untitled". It also shows Add New Milestone to sponsors, which the program rejects (NotADev).
Lists in the app ("Grant Programs: 0" right after creating one) can lag until you reload.
